rag.description: Release a pointer button inside an InvokeInputActions gesture. The step checks the button name before anything is sent, supports five buttons from flow parameters, and ends a press at the current pointer position, so drops, long presses, and clicks finish reliably and no button stays down.

qa.answer: It adds one pointer button release to the input sequence of its InvokeInputActions container.
qa.question: What does the AddPointerUp plugin do?

qa.answer: Button names the button and defaults to Left; Middle, Right, Back, and Forward are accepted, and the plain argument works as well. It stores no outputs.
qa.question: What are the key parameters and outputs of AddPointerUp?

qa.answer: It runs as an InputAction task step with the arrow-pointer icon and the ActionRuleModel, only as a child rule of InvokeInputActions, after the AddPointerDown it ends.
qa.question: How does AddPointerUp fit into an automation workflow?

qa.answer: Release the same button that was pressed, move the pointer to the drop target before releasing, and release held buttons before a flow ends.
qa.question: What are best practices for using AddPointerUp?

qa.answer: Use $type “Action” with pluginName “AddPointerUp”, with no argument for the left button or with {{$ --Button:Right}}, inside the rules of InvokeInputActions.

qa.answer: An unknown button name fails the step, and the container then sends nothing. Outside InvokeInputActions the step fails with a message that names the container.

description: ### Purpose
AddPointerUp releases one pointer button.
It runs only inside InvokeInputActions, and the release happens where the last AddPointerMove action left the pointer.
Flows use it to drop a dragged item, to end a long press, and to complete a click.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature | Description |
| Five buttons | Releases the left, middle, right, back, or forward button. |
| Position from the last move | Releases at the place the pointer was last moved to, which is where a drag drops. |
| Release across groups | Releases a button that an earlier group left down, because the driver keeps the pointer state. |
| Checked before sending | Fails on an unknown button name, and the container then sends nothing. |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case | Description |
| Drag and drop | Release an item over its target to drop it. |
| Long press | Release after a pause to complete a press-and-hold. |
| Clicks at a position | Complete a click that was started at an exact pointer position. |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case | Description |
| Drop handlers | Verify that an item lands in the target when the button is released. |
| Release states | Verify that a pressed style is removed when the button is released. |
| State reset | Return the pointer to a clean state between test cases. |
### Platform
This plugin currently supports **Web** only.
Desktop and mobile drivers are not supported yet.

edge_cases: Pointer is over the wrong target
annotations.expected_result: The left button is up after this action.
annotations.notes: The step runs only inside InvokeInputActions. Releasing a button that is not down is accepted by the driver and changes nothing.

description: ### Release the left button
A rule without an argument releases the left button.
The release happens where the last pointer move left the pointer, which is where a dragged item drops.

annotations.expected_result: The right button is up, and the application opens its context menu.
annotations.notes: Release the same button that was pressed. Button names ignore letter case.

description: ### Release the right button through the Button parameter
The Button parameter names the secondary button.
It completes a right click that an AddPointerDown action started.

edge_cases: Driver does not support the button
annotations.expected_result: The middle button is up after this action.
annotations.notes: Both forms of the argument give the same action. A driver that does not know the button rejects the whole sequence.

description: ### Release the middle button with a plain argument
The plain argument names the button without the parameter form.
It completes a middle click that an AddPointerDown action started.
Names the pointer button to release.
The plain argument of the rule is read as the button when no parameter is used.
Defaults to Left, and any name other than the listed ones fails the step.
parameters.name: Button

description: Releases the main button, which a normal click uses.
It is the default when the rule names no button.
values.name: Left

description: Releases the wheel button.
Browsers use it to open a link in a new tab.
values.name: Middle

description: Releases the secondary button.
Applications use it to open a context menu.
values.name: Right

description: Releases the fourth button, found on the side of some mice.
Browsers use it to go back one page.
values.name: Back

description: Releases the fifth button, found on the side of some mice.
Browsers use it to go forward one page.
values.name: Forward

description: Holds the button, as plain text such as `Right` or as `{{$ --Button:Right}}`.
A rule without an argument uses the left button.
properties.name: Argument

summary: Adds a pointer button release to the sequence of its InvokeInputActions container.
Releases the left button by default, or the middle, right, back, or forward button on request.
Ends a press made by an AddPointerDown action at the current pointer position, which completes a click, a drag, or a long press.
